headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal can expose financial data into Rasa’s allowlisted networked chatbot flow, with prompt-injection and workflow-conflict risks also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP servers and stdin/stdout, so its outputs may be bridged into Rasa conversations or tooling. Rasa’s Messenger/Slack/Twilio-style channels can ingest text that may be treated as instructions if the orchestrator forwards content naively. No direct provenance or isolation is documented for either agent, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal output is forwarded into a Rasa intent or action prompt without provenance tags
IF a shared MCP or chat bridge passes raw text between the agents
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all OpenBBTerminal outputs before forwarding
Disable automatic instruction-following on inbound Rasa messages
Insert a human review step for any cross-agent text handoff
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message schemas between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, while Rasa has allowlisted network egress and multiple external chat surfaces. If the pair shares a workspace or message bus, sensitive financial content can flow from A into B and then out through B’s channels. The profiles do not show encryption, isolation, or redaction by default, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests financial or licensed files and emits them into a shared chat/work queue
IF Rasa relays those messages to external channels such as Slack or Twilio
mitigations: Redact financial identifiers before any handoff to Rasa
Restrict Rasa channels to a test tenant during evaluation
Keep the agents on separate workspaces with no shared files
requires-engineering: add DLP filters on outbound Rasa messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it has little direct write conflict surface. Rasa does not advertise filesystem write either, though it can egress to external channels. The main overlap is read/communication, not concurrent mutation, so conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF a shared bot backend maps both agents onto one state store
mitigations: Separate mutable resources by agent
Run only one writer per shared queue
Document ownership of each channel
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can generate financial analysis that Rasa may present to users through chat channels. If Rasa treats A’s output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into user-facing advice or actions. Because Rasa is a dialogue system and not a verifier by default, the pathway exists in common deployments.
conditions: IF Rasa renders OpenBBTerminal output directly into a user-facing response
IF no validation step checks financial claims before sending the reply
mitigations: Require citation checks before Rasa replies
Mark OpenBBTerminal output as untrusted in the prompt
Add a confidence threshold for user-facing financial claims
requires-engineering: route high-impact outputs to a review queue

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, while Rasa handles text/voice over external messaging channels. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, residency, or licensing if the same data class is forwarded from A into B. The profiles do not document aligned controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is forwarded from OpenBBTerminal into Rasa channels
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through Rasa channels
Set short retention on chat transcripts
Review licensing terms for any forwarded market data
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
